tools.description: Answer a question using web-grounded AI (Perplexity Agent API, fast preset). Best for: quick factual questions, summaries, explanations, and general Q&A. Returns a text response with numbered citations. Fastest and cheapest option. Supports filtering by recency (hour/day/week/month/year), domain restrictions, and search token budgets. For in-depth multi-source research, use perplexity_research instead. For step-by-step reasoning and analysis, use perplexity_reason instead.

max_tokens.description: Maximum total search-context tokens, not generated answer tokens. Overrides the legacy search_context_size total budget.

max_tokens_per_page.description: Maximum search-context tokens extracted per result page. Overrides the legacy search_context_size per-page budget.

search_context_size.description: Deprecated compatibility shorthand for search token budgets: low=2000/512, medium=4000/1024, high=8000/2048 (total/per-page). Explicit max_tokens and max_tokens_per_page override these defaults.

search_domain_filter.description: Restrict search results to specific domains (e.g., ['wikipedia.org', 'arxiv.org']). Use '-' prefix for exclusion (e.g., ['-reddit.com']).

search_recency_filter.description: Filter search results by recency. Use 'hour' for very recent news, 'day' for today's updates, 'week' for this week, etc.

tools.name: perplexity_ask

tools.description: Fetch web pages by URL through the Perplexity Context API. Best for: reading pages when you already have the URLs. Returns Markdown by default. Can also return HTML, links, the passages most relevant to a query (highlights), and yes or no scores for your questions (criteria). Every result with status ok or not_modified includes page metadata. Full pages can be long; to get specific facts, set formats to ['highlights'] and set highlights.query. To find URLs, use perplexity_search instead.

cache_only.description: When true, read only stored copies and never fetch live (default: false). A URL with no stored copy returns status no_content. Requires max_age_seconds above 0. Cannot be combined with snapshot_as_of.

criteria.description: Optional descriptions of what makes the answer true and what makes it false

false.description: What makes the answer false (1-500 characters)

true.description: What makes the answer true (1-500 characters)

instructions.description: The yes or no question to answer, or the statement to check (1-1000 characters)

criteria.description: Yes or no questions to score each page with (1-5 questions). An object keyed by question ID. Each value is an object with type 'noul', the question in instructions, and optionally a nested criteria object that says what makes the answer true or false (e.g., {"is_changelog": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Is this page a product changelog?", "criteria": {"true": "The page lists dated releases.", "false": "The page is not a list of releases."}}}). IDs must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}. 'query' is reserved, and this tool does not accept '__proto__'. Each answer is a probability of yes from 0 to 1. Scoring does not filter or reorder results.

formats.description: What to return for each page (default: ['markdown']). Every result with status ok or not_modified includes metadata, so do not list it; pass [] for metadata only. 'highlights' also requires the highlights object.

highlights.description: Settings for the 'highlights' format. Whenever you set this, also set formats to include 'highlights' (e.g., formats: ['highlights']). A request that sets highlights fails if formats is omitted or does not include 'highlights'.

max_tokens_per_url.description: Maximum length of each page's highlights in tokens (1-4096, default: 1024)

query.description: What to look for in each page (1-1024 characters)

if_modified_since.description: A metadata last_modified value from an earlier result, in IMF-fixdate form (e.g., 'Thu, 03 Dec 1992 08:37:20 GMT'). Requires exactly one URL and max_age_seconds 0. A page that has not changed returns status not_modified and no content.

max_age_seconds.description: Maximum age in seconds of a stored copy to accept (0-63072000, default: 172800). 0 always fetches the page live. Cannot be combined with snapshot_as_of.

snapshot_as_of.description: Return each page as stored at or before this RFC 3339 time with a time zone (e.g., '2026-11-01T00:00:00Z'). Must not be in the future or more than 365 days ago. Never fetches live. Cannot be combined with max_age_seconds, cache_only, or if_modified_since.

timeout_ms.description: Time budget in milliseconds for fetching the pages (1000-110000). A URL that does not finish in time returns status crawl_timeout.

urls.description: http or https URLs to fetch (1-50). Each URL gets its own result and status.

tools.name: perplexity_context

tools.description: Analyze a question using step-by-step reasoning with web grounding (Perplexity Agent API, medium preset). Best for: math, logic, comparisons, complex arguments, and tasks requiring chain-of-thought. Returns a reasoned response with numbered citations. Supports filtering by recency (hour/day/week/month/year), domain restrictions, and search token budgets. For quick factual questions, use perplexity_ask instead. For comprehensive multi-source research, use perplexity_research instead.

max_tokens.description: Maximum total search-context tokens, not generated answer tokens. Overrides the legacy search_context_size total budget.

max_tokens_per_page.description: Maximum search-context tokens extracted per result page. Overrides the legacy search_context_size per-page budget.

search_context_size.description: Deprecated compatibility shorthand for search token budgets: low=2000/512, medium=4000/1024, high=8000/2048 (total/per-page). Explicit max_tokens and max_tokens_per_page override these defaults.

search_domain_filter.description: Restrict search results to specific domains (e.g., ['wikipedia.org', 'arxiv.org']). Use '-' prefix for exclusion (e.g., ['-reddit.com']).

search_recency_filter.description: Filter search results by recency. Use 'hour' for very recent news, 'day' for today's updates, 'week' for this week, etc.

tools.name: perplexity_reason

tools.description: Conduct deep, multi-source research on a topic (Perplexity Agent API, high preset). Best for: literature reviews, comprehensive overviews, investigative queries needing many sources. Returns a detailed response with numbered citations. Significantly slower than other tools (can take minutes). For quick factual questions, use perplexity_ask instead. For logical analysis and reasoning, use perplexity_reason instead.
tools.name: perplexity_research

tools.description: Search the web and return a ranked list of results with titles, URLs, snippets, and dates. Best for: finding specific URLs, checking recent news, verifying facts, discovering sources. Returns formatted results (title, URL, snippet, date) with no AI synthesis. Supports recency filters, domain restrictions, and a lower-latency fast search mode. For AI-generated answers with citations, use perplexity_ask instead.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for regional results (e.g., 'US', 'GB')

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-20, default: 10)

max_tokens_per_page.description: Maximum tokens to extract per webpage (default: 1024)

search_domain_filter.description: Restrict search results to specific domains (e.g., ['wikipedia.org', 'arxiv.org']). Use '-' prefix for exclusion (e.g., ['-reddit.com']).

search_recency_filter.description: Filter search results by recency. Use 'hour' for very recent news, 'day' for today's updates, 'week' for this week, etc.

search_type.description: Search backend. 'web' (default) is the standard web search. 'fast' is lower latency and lower cost; prefer it for routine lookups inside agent loops, and keep 'web' for rare or ambiguous questions.

tools.name: perplexity_search
